candidates.instrument: NYISO P-35 Real-Time Events + P-25 Operational Announcements
candidates.reason: INERT — the mechanism's own driver does not occur at NYISO in the training window. Across all three years and 5347 published operational messages there are 0 Maximum Generation declarations and 0 emergency-energy alerts; the single 'major emergency state' entry (2025) is a system-state change, not a MaxGen window with a tier price. A declared-window offer floor with no declared window is inert by construction (rule 17 [R-FLOOR-WINDOW]). Separately, the NYISO-native analogues of the phenomenon are ALREADY armed as distinct mechanisms — reserve scarcity through the RCPF families and demand response through nyiso_scr_edrp — so arming a third would stack on both (rule 19 [R-ONE-MECH]). Recorded observation, NOT opened here: the log does carry 126-195 reserve pick-up events a year, which belongs to the everyday-reserve-formation question nyiso-110 adjudicated.

candidates.reason: GOVERNANCE-REFUSED on identification, not on fit, and not by analogy. Both mechanisms are identified from SUBMITTED unit-level offer curves, and NYISO publishes no such disclosure — the repo's own record establishes this twice over: 'NYISO publishes no 60-Day-DAM equivalent' (docs/calibration-log/nyiso.md, the nyiso-87 gas-bridge derivation, which is why that mechanism's min-load had to be reconstructed from CAMPD loading-when-on instead) and 'NYISO publishes no submitted-curve equivalent' (docs/mechanism-testing-matrix.md). There is no offer or bid artifact for NYISO anywhere under data/raw/. CAMPD gives what a unit DID, never what it BID, so no NYISO source can identify an offer LEVEL. The only remaining way to arm either is to carry the donor's fitted offer level across the ISO boundary, which rule 25 [R-ISO-SCOPE] forbids outright — and measured_offer_surface has already failed to transfer twice (PJM R, NEISO I). G rather than U: this is refused, not merely untested. Re-openable only by a NEW NYISO offer-data source, which is what 'new evidence' would mean for this cell under rule 28a.

GOVERNANCE-REFUSED under rule 19 [R-ONE-MECH]: NYISO already has a mechanism for this exact phenomenon, ARMED ON THE KEEPER. nyiso_import_hub_prices=True reprices every import-node tranche at the MEASURED hourly neighbor system LMP (PJM_west at the PJM DA hub mean, ISONE_tie at the ISO-NE DA hub mean, the residual scarcity block at the hourly max of the two, each plus the inter-control-area wheeling hurdle, with the export sink repriced at max minus hurdle so the seam is arbitrage-free). Its own docstring names it 'the NYISO analogue of miso_pjm_lmp_import_pricing and caiso_import_hub_prices' — i.e. it IS the transfer of this family, already made and already promoted. Arming reference_price_interface on top would price the neighbor seam twice. Rule 14 [R-ACCURATE] also orders the two for a BACKCAST: the armed mechanism uses the neighbours' MEASURED hourly prices, while a reference-price interface is the forward-grade construct for years where no measured neighbour price exists. The measured one dominates in-window. NOTE FOR THE FORECAST LANE, not decided here: the fc cell is a different question, because in a forecast year there IS no measured neighbour LMP and the forward-grade seam is the natural former — that belongs to the forecast programme, not to a backcast calibration session.

INERT BY MAGNITUDE, on NYISO's own fleet rather than by analogy. The mechanism re-times a battery fleet's month-of-COD phase-in, so its maximum possible effect is bounded by the within-window growth it re-times. NYISO's lithium-ion fleet moves 200.5 -> 252.7 MW across the whole training window — 52.2 MW — and its pumped storage is FLAT at 1,220 MW (Blenheim-Gilboa, in service since 1973, so it carries no vintage question at all). Placing the entire increment half a year wrong at a generous 0.25 capacity factor mis-allocates at most 0.0572 TWh against ~150 TWh of annual NYISO load — below the resolution of every scored criterion. The donors are the reason the mechanism exists and the reason it does not transfer: ERCOT and CAISO added battery capacity in this window two to three ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE larger than NYISO's 53 MW, where month-grain timing genuinely moves prices. Same verdict class as nyiso-113's measured_ramp_capability (U -> I on a 18.8x headroom margin): arithmetic, not a solve. Re-openable if NYISO's battery build accelerates — the bound above is the test to re-run, not a permanent finding.
